title: Video Hearing Calendar: Block Gap Table for Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
**Unemployment Insurance Appeals — video hearing calendar.** A video session is placed on the Department's video hearing calendar a number of calendar days after the hearing date set on the appeal; that number is the *video block gap*. It turns on two things: the latest interpreter request on the appeal (the one with the most recent request date) and the hearing length of the appeal's docket.

**Rule.** The video block gap is the long video block days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for a language other than Spanish and the docket's hearing length is at least the long hearing minutes, the short video block days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for a language other than Spanish and the docket's hearing length is shorter than the long hearing minutes, and the standard video block days when the latest interpreter request is for Spanish or no interpreter is requested.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Long video block | 10 calendar days |
| Short video block | 7 calendar days |
| Standard video block | 5 calendar days |
| Long hearing threshold | 60 minutes |

## The gap as a matrix

| Latest interpreter request | Docket hearing length 60 minutes or more | Docket hearing length under 60 minutes |
|---|---|---|
| a language other than Spanish (American Sign Language included) | 10 days | 7 days |
| Spanish | 5 days | 5 days |
| no interpreter requested | 5 days | 5 days |

## By docket

The docket hearing lengths are: Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue 60 minutes; Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue 45; Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination 45; Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud 60; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge 60; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate 90; Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review 0 (no hearing). Hence, where the latest request is for a language other than Spanish:

| Docket | Hearing length | Video block gap |
|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | 60 | 10 days |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | 45 | 7 days |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | 45 | 7 days |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | 60 | 10 days |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | 60 | 10 days |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | 90 | 10 days |

*Boundary:* a hearing length of exactly 60 minutes is "at least the long hearing minutes" and takes the long block; 45 minutes is shorter and takes the short block.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* on a Separation Issue appeal whose interpreter requests were Spanish (2 April) and then Haitian Creole (9 April), the latest request is not Spanish and the docket runs 60 minutes, so the block gap is 10 days. Had the later request been the Spanish one, it would be 5 days.
